transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kline (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Hannah Park (Redwood SE), Sam Lee (Aurora CTO), Nina Patel (Head of InfoSec), Omar Ruiz (Cloud Architect), Maya Chen (Compliance)

Auto-Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Discussed BYOK flows, HSM failover, escrow, SOC 2/ISO artifacts, RBAC controls, and audit log retention. Agreed to perf tests and documentation handoff.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about an hour. quick round robin real quick please say role.
00:08 Sam: Sam Lee, CTO, Aurora Mortgages — hi.
00:12 Nina: Nina Patel, Head of InfoSec.
00:15 Omar: Omar Ruiz, cloud arch.
00:18 Maya: Maya Chen, compliance.
00:21 Jordan: Great thanks. Priya and Hannah from my side will cover HSM/BYOK details and a short failure-mode playbook, yeah.
00:29 Priya: Hi all, yes im Priya, SE, I can start with a high level of how Redwood supports customer managed keys and the HSM options. Note some of the naming in recordings might be off — redwood has two paths: hosted with BYOK (tenant key wrapping) and private (VPC) deploy using customer HSM connectors.
00:50 Nina: Quick clarifying Q: we need keys never leave our control, and we need dual control, is that supported?
00:56 Priya: Short answer yes. We support a BYOK flow where you import a wrapping key into our KMS connector which is backed by an HSM — if you choose HSM-on-prem we'll use a connector and key wrapping, keys never stored in plaintext in Redwood control plane. Dual-control and split knowledge can be supported via key escrow and KMS ACLs. I'll explain details.
01:18 Omar: When you say connector is that an agent or a proxy? does it originate outbound connections only?
01:25 Hannah: It's an outbound TLS tunnel from your VPC to our connector endpoint — so it initiates from your network. We don't open inbound ports. The connector handles wrapping/unwrapping requests and hardware-backed key ops stay on your HSM if you're using on-prem HSM.
01:42 Sam: Ok, breakout: performance — does using external HSM add noticeable latency per token? Our SLAs are tight for quote generation in the app.
01:51 Priya: Good question. For token-level crypto we keep the actual model inference unaffected — key ops are mostly during session initialization and cache priming. If you do per-token signing that's different but not typical. For typical encrypt-at-rest/KV cache wrapping the additional latency is minimal — we've seen an average 20-80ms for first unwrap depending on HSM. For streaming there's rarely a per-token hop. We'll quantify with a perf test.
02:18 Nina: About audit logs — we need an immutable trail for key operations with user attribution and SSO identity mapping. How do you capture that?
02:27 Priya: Redwood produces detailed audit logs that include KMS operations, key IDs, requester principal, and request metadata. When you integrate SSO/SAML we map principals to your IdP identities and can push logs to your SIEM via syslog or API. Retention configurable — default 1 year, options to extend.
02:46 Omar: Are those logs tamper-evident? chain-of-custody?
02:50 Hannah: We support append-only log sinks and can integrate with your WORM storage. For higher assurances we support signed log bundles and can provide periodic integrity proofs. It's not a full blockchain but we can do HMAC-signed batched logs.
03:08 Maya: For compliance we need SOC 2 scope artifacts and ISO 27001 evidence tied to the key lifecycle. Do you have canned artifacts?
03:14 Jordan: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II report and a packet with control mappings related to key management — we'll share that. For ISO we'll provide our Statement of Applicability and the key lifecycle controls mappings. I will add that to the follow-ups.
03:30 Nina: On key rotation: we currently rotate customer master keys every 90 days and need proof of rotation + ability to force rotate immediately if compromise suspected. What does Redwood support?
03:40 Priya: We support scheduled rotation cadence configurable down to daily, and manual rotation via API. Rotations can be staged: we can do double-wrap approach and support re-encrypt jobs for existing objects. We'll include runbooks for emergency rotation.
03:55 Sam: Escrow and forensics — if we deprovision an admin or in incident response need material keys handed off how do you manage escrow?
04:03 Priya: Multiple options: you can retain an escrow copy in your HSM, we can hold encrypted escrow under tenant-managed wrapping key, or a third-party escrow. We do support notarized key handoff workflows (two-person approval) and have tooling to record the handoff event in the audit trail.
04:21 Nina: HSM high-availability: we require defined RTO and RPO. If primary HSM goes down, how do you failover without exposing key material?
04:29 Hannah: We recommend a geo-redundant HSM cluster with multi-site replication. For on-prem you can configure active-passive HSM pairs and use a secondary HSM in another region — failover uses rewrapped keys and TLS-authenticated connector endpoints. The failover process uses encrypted key shares — keys aren't exported in plaintext.
04:50 Omar: That sounds fine but are there cross-region export restrictions? we have EU residency constraints for EU customers.
04:56 Priya: For data residency, you can pin keys to a specific region. Redeployment and failover can be restricted to the same region, or to an isolated DR site inside your jurisdiction. We'll document options.
05:10 Maya: Do you support hardware-backed KMS like AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, or on-prem Thales/Entrust?
05:16 Priya: Yes, we integrate with common HSMs (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) and PKCS#11-compatible on-prem HSMs (Thales, Utimaco, SafeNet). Connector supports PKCS#11 and KMIP where applicable.
05:32 Sam: Let's talk about key wrapping patterns — do you recommend tenant-level master keys or per-application keys?
05:38 Hannah: We recommend tenant master key (TMK) for high-level separation, with per-app data keys (DEKs) derived and rotated frequently. That limits blast radius and aligns with compliance. We can automate DEK rotation and rewrap on key rotation.
05:52 Nina: Who can request unwraps, and how is RBAC enforced?
05:56 Priya: RBAC is integrated with your IdP — roles map to KMS ACLs. Requester principal is asserted via SAML/OIDC token; you can require MFA or step-up for sensitive operations. We also support policy-based access (attributes like environment, region, service).
06:14 Omar: For testing the connector, what network egress rules are needed?
06:18 Hannah: Outbound HTTPS to our connector endpoints (list shared in a doc), port 443. We recommend allowlist to those endpoints. No inbound.
06:25 Sam: Ok good. On escrow: can we have a split-key escrow where part stays on-prem and part with Redwood?
06:29 Priya: Yes, that's the split-knowledge model. You can keep a key share inside your HSM and Redwood holds an encrypted share — only reconstructed with two-party approval. We have runbooks for split-key recovery.
06:42 Maya: About encryption at rest for model caches: are caches encrypted separately or rely on storage encryption?
06:47 Priya: We encrypt model KV caches with DEKs which are themselves wrapped by TMKs. Storage-level encryption is additional layer; we recommend both. Caches can be configured to use in-memory encryption keys derived at startup for extra protection.
07:02 Sam: Compliance question: does Redwood produce artifacts we can submit to regulators showing the chain — like key lifecycle logs that demonstrate rotation and deletion?
07:09 Jordan: Yes, we have exportable audit bundles with timestamps, requestor identity, KMS operation type, and object references. We can provide attested logs for a given period.
07:18 Nina: Are deletion operations cryptographically assured? if we delete a wrapped key, can you guarantee object data can't be unwrapped?
07:25 Priya: When you delete the TMK and all key material and caches are rewrapped, we mark objects as unrecoverable unless escrowed. We provide crypto-shredding documentation and can run verification jobs to ensure keys are gone. Note: backups need to be handled — if there are copies encrypted with old keys, you'll want rewrap or destruction flows.
07:48 Omar: Is there an option for FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSM only?
07:52 Hannah: Yes, we can require FIPS-validated modules in our path and will only accept modules with FIPS certificates for production keys. We'll capture that in the onboarding checklist.
08:02 Sam: Let's surface a couple of tricky scenarios: 1) Key compromise on customer HSM, 2) Redwood control plane compromised — how do we handle each?
08:12 Priya: If customer HSM compromised: rotate TMK in HSM, revoke old key IDs in Redwood, rewrap DEKs, run forensic export, and if needed failover to alternate HSM. If Redwood control plane compromised: because you use BYOK and keys aren't in plaintext, the attacker would still need your wrapping key. We have layered defense — but we'll also revoke connectors, rotate keys, and provide a forensic package. Both flows are in our incident response playbook.
08:44 Nina: What about escrow key handoff in legal situations — do you support court-ordered access?
08:49 Jordan: We treat legal requests seriously; we have a process and will notify customers per contract, but we don't hold plaintext keys without tenant consent or court order. For enterprises, recommended path is to manage escrow on your side or use a third-party escrow to avoid surprise disclosures.
09:06 Maya: For audits we may want a hands-on demo of rotation and log export — can we do a 2-hr workshop?
09:10 Jordan: Absolutely, we can schedule an onboarding workshop with an SE-run live demo. Priya, Hannah, availability?
09:16 Priya: We can do week of Jan 26. Hannah: same.
09:19 Jordan: Great.
09:22 (---discussion continues, deeper technical)
09:50 Priya: Quick note on key derivation and cache: our runtime keeps decrypted DEKs only in protected memory and uses hardware-backed enclaves where available. We also maintain per-epoch keys for short lived sessions to limit exposure. The cache prefix is never stored with full key material.
10:18 Omar: For regional residency: do you support dedicated private deployments in EU region that don't call back to our US control plane?
10:26 Hannah: Yes — Redwood Private allows a customer-managed control plane in their VPC with no outbound control plane egress if that's required. We can package an on-prem console or VPC-deployed control plane. That will be part of the Private engagement.
10:40 Sam: Cost tradeoffs: what incremental cost do we expect for BYOK with HSM vs hosted default?
10:46 Priya: HSM and BYOK add connector and HSM usage costs; there's also engineering overhead for onboarding. In rough ballpark: 10-30% increase in unit cost depending on HSM vendor and replication. We'll provide a cost estimate based on your projected QPS.
11:02 Nina: Question about SSO: we require SCIM group sync and SAML. Do you support attribute-based access?
11:09 Jordan: Yes, SAML + SCIM for provisioning; ABAC via SAML attributes, role mapping to KMS ACLs, step-up via authentication context.
11:18 Maya: For retention, we need logs kept for 7 years for some regulatory lanes; can Redwood forward logs to our archival bucket?
11:25 Hannah: Yes, we can push to your S3/GCS/Azure archive. Retention policy can be yours; we can also mirror logs to your SIEM and to our long-term archive for joint retrieval.
11:37 Sam: Any known limitations in the current connector for throughput?
11:40 Priya: Connector scales horizontally; bottleneck is HSM TPS. If you need high TPS we recommend CloudHSM with autoscaled pools or distributed HSM clusters. We'll run the staged test.
11:52 Jordan: Ok let's outline immediate next steps — Priya will run perf test using Aurora payload, I'll share BYOK playbook and SOC2 artifacts, Maya will confirm residency doc, Omar will share rotation cadence.
12:03 Sam: Great, and we'll prepare a whitelist ruleset to share.
12:08 Nina: Also please include the failure-mode runbook for legal/key escrow scenarios.
12:14 Jordan: Noted. Anything else?
12:18 Maya: One more: can we enforce a policy that no plaintext keys are ever logged by Redwood?
12:23 Priya: Absolutely — we redact key material from logs and include that in the control mapping.
12:30 Jordan: Perfect. We'll send a calendar invite for the workshop. Thanks everyone.
12:35 (meeting end)

Post-meeting notes: Attendees requested tangible artifacts and an operational run of the connector. Action items captured above. Transcription contains occasional minor mis-hearings (e.g., PKCS"11" read as PK-CS eleven).
